jobs.description: Employer: CSUN 10482 - Office of Basic Needs Expires: 10/04/2026 Student Volunteer Coordinator – Office of Basic NeedsThe Basic Needs office provides and refers to services and resources to remove barriers and empower students to persist and thrive in their educational journey towards academic success. Basic Needs staff guide students to identify and access short- and long-term, sustainable solutions in an effort to successfully graduate from CSUN. POSITION DESCRIPTIONUnder general supervision from the Senior Food Programs Care Coordinator, the Student Volunteer Coordinator for the Office of Basic Needs will support multiple program areas, including the CSUN Food Pantry, Basic Needs Outreach, MataBites, and other Basic Needs initiatives. This position serves as the central coordinator for all experiential learning participants, overseeing onboarding, placement, communication, and administrative processes for volunteers, interns, service learners, and College Corps members to ensure consistency across programs. SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES Communicate engagement opportunities to the campus community Serve as a liaison to faculty and campus partnersCoordinate placements for all interested individuals across programs (CSUN Food Pantry, CalFresh Outreach, Nourish to Flourish, MataBites, Basic Needs Outreach, etc…). Schedule and interview interested individuals to evaluate fit and placement.Maintain accurate and timely records of volunteers, interns, service learners and College Corps members placed with the Office, including but not limited to resumes, interviews, on-boarding, mid-term and final evaluation documents.Track hours, evaluations, and compliance requirementsAssist with responding to all volunteer inquiries via phone, text, email, etc.Provide ongoing support, guidance, and communication to volunteers, interns, and service learners to ensure clarity of roles and expectationsEnsure consistency across all experiential learning rolesIdentify areas for improvement in placement, onboarding, and engagement processes and provide recommendations to program staffOperate various office equipment: multiple-line phones, data entry, sending emails, copying and scanning documents, etc.Use remote collaboration tools including Zoom, Adobe Sign, Box, Google Drive, Microsoft Office, etc.Prepare office correspondence and other documents with Microsoft OfficeProcess work accurately, self-manage workflow.Perform other related duties as assigned.SKILLS DESIREDFlexible, adaptable, open to changing and learning, willingness to adjust when necessary for work in a multi-faceted, diverse, and evolving team environment.Self-motivated self-starter capable of initiating tasks independently.Takes direction, well-organized, handles multiple ongoing tasks at once.Highly communicative, ability to connect and follow up with other staff members and their programmatic needs.Detail oriented and attentive to minutiae.Ability to manage multiple priorities. Use of critical thinking skills with discretion in judgment and decision-making.Capable of providing insight and suggestions on how best to reach the student population. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:General:Minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher maintained throughout entire time of service Demonstrable knowledge of the following:Microsoft Office suite of products including Word, Adobe Sign, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook.Technology as it relates to personal computer, smart devices, and Zoom personal meeting software.Utility and functionality of basic office equipment (copy, fax, phone).How to clearly express ideas and directions verbally and in writing.How to establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with students, student organizations, faculty, staff, administrators, and surrounding community. EXPECTATIONSPassion for volunteerism and connecting with the community.Ability to reach with arms and use hands to finger, handle, or feel.Ability to stoop, kneel, crouch, crawl, or occasionally sit for extended periods.Willingness to work in both indoor and outdoor environments in possible inclement weather conditions.Willingness to work occasional weekends and evenings.Willingness to learn new software required for tasks. Mindful with the ability to respond appropriately to sensitive/personal matters. OTHER CONSIDERATIONSExperience working in an office setting preferred.Experience working with volunteers and organizing community members preferred. GENERAL INFORMATIONAreas concerning eligibility, hours of work, the classification for student employees, and salary are in alignment with the University’s Office of Human Resources (HR) and the “Student Assistant Work-Study Salary Schedule.” Classification: Student Assistant Level IIIJobs assigned to Level II work under general supervision. This means that definite work objectives are set for the employee but methods of performing the tasks are frequently left to the judgment of the employee with occasional instruction or advice provided by the supervisor. The frequency of review by the supervisor depends on the difficulty and complexity of the assignment or on the impact or result of the work performed. While the supervisor is again responsible for the general assignment of work, less control may be exercised over the flow for work and instructions given may be more general in nature. The employee is responsible for the results of the work. Jobs assigned to this level usually require some previous experience, education, or specialized skill. SalaryThis position will start at $17.00 per hour. Hours of Work:This position requires commitment to a set schedule each week during operational business hours 8 AM – 5 PM Monday through Friday (Wednesday and Thursday operating until 7pm). Students are not to exceed 20 hours of work in an academic week. Position is year-round including Summer, Winter and Spring break while the campus is open. Per HR, the following information more fully explains the guidelines which must be adhered to as a student employee on campus:1. Generally, students shall be given a 15-minute break during a 4-hour shift, and at least a 30-minute break for lunch during a 6-hour shift. The 15-minute break is paid time; the 30-minute lunch is unpaid time. The 15-minute break cannot be accumulated for lunch and cannot alter the normal work schedule. 2. During the Academic Semester (please see CSUN campus academic calendar), Student Assistants may work up to, but not in excess of 20 hours per week total in all positions. When the academic semester starts in the middle of a work week it is a “split” week. For example, when the beginning of the semester is on a Wednesday, the 1st two days of week are still in the "Break" time period can be full-time, while the remaining days of the week would be under the restriction to work half- time. One Example is:Monday = 8 hoursTuesday = 8 hoursWednesday = 4 hoursThursday = 4 hoursFriday = 4 hoursTotal hours that can be worked in this “split” week scenario is 28 hours.The actual hours per day worked in that week can be in any combination resulting in the slightly higher than 20 hours per week cap. 3. The CSU policy restricts student assistant work time. In addition, the Internal Revenue Service guidelines for student assistants to remain exempt from social security and Medicare deductions, limits their normal working hours to 20 during the school year. An exception is allowed during winter inter-session, spring break, and summer session, or if the hours exceed 20 for a short period of time and infrequently. The CSU policy states that it is permissible for student assistants to work up to 30 hours in a week when enrolled in classes, only under emergency or other unusual situations. Exceptions to this policy require approval of the Financial Manager (MPP Administrator) in each department or College. While the exception may be granted on an emergency basis, frequent use of the exception will result in Human Resources review and contact with the department and/or college.

jobs.description: Employer: CSUN 10052 - Information Technology Expires: 10/17/2026 IT Project Management Intern California State University, Northridge – Division of Information Technology, Project Management Department: IT Governance and EngagementReports to: Celene Valenzuela (Assistant Director of Governance and Engagement) Duration: Fall 2026 Semester (18 weeks)Work Hours: Up to 20 hours/week Position OverviewWithin the Division of Information Technology, as a member of the IT Project Management Office (IT PMO), the intern will gain hands-on experience applying enterprise systems and project management concepts to active technology projects that support CSUN’s students, faculty, and staff. The IT PMO uses a common framework for how IT projects—small, intermediate, and large—are proposed, planned, executed, controlled, and closed, including shared tools, templates, and governance processes. Under the guidance of the Assistant Director and working closely with the Project Manager leading the ServiceNow enterprise platform (and related systems), the intern will support project leads from initial intake and deep-dive planning meetings through project completion, helping to organize work, track progress, and document outcomes. This internship is designed to reinforce project organization and staffing, planning and scheduling (PERT/CPM concepts), control, budgeting awareness, quality, and project environments across campus units—while giving the student direct exposure to major enterprise IT initiatives in a structured PMO environment. The intern will also observe and use current enterprise and project management tools in practice. Key Responsibilities IT PMO Framework, Enterprise Systems, & Deep Dive SupportParticipate in IT PMO deep dive sessions where the project sponsor and assigned project leads review the project’s purpose, goals, scope, key team members, major milestones, assumptions, and potential risks using the IT PMO project playbook.Observe how projects of different sizes (small enhancements, intermediate rollouts, and large implementations) are evaluated for strategic alignment, feasibility, cost–benefit, risk, dependencies, and governance review within an enterprise systems context (e.g., ServiceNow and other campus platforms).Capture and organize meeting notes, decisions, risks, and action items from deep dive and other planning meetings; ensure that project playbooks and related artifacts are documented and stored in the IT PMO repository. Project Organization, Planning, Scheduling (PERT/CPM Concepts), and ControlWork with an IT Project Manager to build and maintain project schedules, reinforcing concepts such as task sequencing, dependencies, and critical paths, and supporting the Project Manager throughout the project lifecycle.Help identify and document roles and responsibilities for project team members, reflecting project organization and staffing principles.Monitor progress against the plan and follow up with team members on upcoming deadlines and deliverables, contributing to schedule and scope control. Governance, Budget Awareness, and Quality SupportAssist the Assistant Director in preparing updates for IT Leadership and CSUN Technology Governance, including materials for monthly IT Leadership PMO project portfolio updates where progress is reviewed and roadblocks are surfaced for support.Develop a basic understanding of how budget, effort, and resource constraints influence project decisions, timelines, and prioritization (no direct budget authority, but exposure to how these factors are considered).Support quality-focused activities such as tracking issues, documenting acceptance criteria, and helping summarize key quality and performance outcomes after major releases. Project Environments and ReportingContribute to the preparation of concise project status updates for IT Leadership and governance bodies, learning how to tailor information to different stakeholders and escalation paths. Project Close-Out, Metrics, Hypercare, and DocumentationSupport the PMO and project leads in formal project close-out, including documenting outcomes versus goals, collecting basic usage/impact metrics, and capturing key lessons learned.Help monitor the Hypercare period (typically 2–4 weeks after launch), track issues and enhancement requests for enterprise systems, and confirm that key items are resolved or transitioned into ongoing support processes.Help organize and archive project documentation (charters, schedules, status reports, close-out summaries, and lessons learned) in the central SharePoint location for future reference and reuse on subsequent projects. Important NotesThis is an unpaid internship for educational purposes only.
